narrative.overview:
Kingdom Network is a working marketplace first: crisp, candid, and visibly populated. Its opening gives individuals immediate search and a photographed, priced pathway; the same page gives churches a full dark-green marketplace, dedicated profiles, and a high-contrast partner-acquisition close. It should feel like a serious global commerce platform built around church authority, not a ministry brochure with products added later.

The language is modern and unornamented. One self-hosted Nohemi family carries everything from large propositions to metadata. Real clergy, study, and congregation photography provides humanity and issuer context; black and white provide hard structure; ministry green establishes trust; lime marks high-value acquisition; cream and pale blue separate the journey without fragmenting it.
keyCharacteristics: One self-hosted Nohemi voice across every UI role
Dense, four-column photographic product inventory on wide screens
Equal marketplace weight for products and verified churches
Black, white, ministry green, lime, cream, and pale-blue color blocking
Explicit pathway, issuer, requirement, price, and verification information
API-backed inventory with real product, church, account, and interest states

rules.name: The Green Means Ministry Rule
rules.body: Use ministry green for issuer authority, verified relationships, and meaningful completion—not as an arbitrary decorative accent.

rules.name: The Lime Closes the Loop Rule
rules.body: Lime belongs to acquisition, confirmation, and decisive participation moments; keep it scarce enough to feel actionable.

rules.name: The Field Change Rule
rules.body: Cream introduces discovery, green establishes the church marketplace, pale blue explains progression, and black closes with partner acquisition.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Every interface role uses Nohemi. Do not introduce serif, script, or platform-default type for artificial ceremony.

rules.name: The Weight Does the Work Rule
rules.body: Use semibold and bold to separate proposition, inventory, metadata, and action while keeping the family unified.

rules.name: The Inventory Has Density Rule
rules.body: Wide screens show four products across with compact metadata; do not inflate cards into sparse promotional tiles.

rules.name: The Churches Are Inventory Rule
rules.body: Churches receive a full marketplace field, photographic cards, detail routes, specialties, verification, and offering shelves—not a secondary logo strip.

rules.name: The Flat Marketplace Rule
rules.body: Prefer color blocking, borders, and image cropping to shadows. Do not make inventory float like app widgets.

dos: Do keep type, issuer, verification, duration, level, rating, reviews, and price in one compact scan path.
Do treat churches as browsable inventory with imagery, specialties, offering counts, and dedicated routes.
Do use locally hosted Nohemi for every UI role.
Do represent loading, empty, error, disabled, success, demonstration, and database states honestly.
Do retain the explicit visa disclaimer wherever invitation documents appear.
donts: Don't replace real clergy and congregation photography with gradients, seals, icons, or invented partner marks.
Don't inflate the product catalog into oversized lifestyle cards that reduce comparison density.
Don't demote church acquisition to a footer link or make churches subordinate to individual offerings.
Don't introduce serif typography, ornamental ecclesiastical styling, or soft SaaS-dashboard shadows.
Don't imply sign-in exists when it does not, hide MongoDB submission states, or present demonstration records as production data.
Don't imply an invitation document guarantees a visa or immigration decision.
